classification.difficultyReason: Every part is the same direct procedure: swap x and y, then rearrange. Most parts need one or two inversion steps. The hardest are n, which needs a divide, then a cube root of a fraction, and k, which comes as an implicit linear equation and must be rearranged. Parts i and o also take a short multi-step rearrangement. There are no restrictions, no domain or range work, no graphing and no interpretation, and the method is signposted by the prompt. This is more than the single-step angle fact in A2, because of the multi-step rearrangements and the cube-root and implicit forms. It is below p9-q4, which also needs graphing a circle, reflecting it and reasoning about domain and range.
